items.title: Why Ireland Is So Vulnerable to Russian Threats | WSJ
items.author: The Wall Street Journal
items.content:
<article>Ireland is a small country with huge global significance; around 75% of all transatlantic subsea cables pass through or near its waters. However the historically neutral country has the lowest level of defense spending in the European Union. As more Russian-linked vessels transit through its waters, Ireland’s government has vowed to increase spending.

WSJ’s Sune Engel Rasmussen joins the Irish Navy as it tries to safeguard its seas.
